limitations: READ_ONLY lane: no service was started, stopped, restarted, enabled or disabled; no flag/HALT/budget/gates.json/ledger was written; no file was deleted, moved, renamed or overwritten. mutations_performed = 0.

journalctl on 138 required sudo -n; user-scope systemctl over ssh is broken on 138 ($DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS unset) so all unit state was read from SYSTEM scope, where the octopus units actually live (User=ari).
182/193 have no timedatectl, so NTPSynchronized could not be read there; clock coherence was instead measured by the midpoint method (max |drift| 0.36s).

The 182 fire-loop's start timestamp (2026-09-17T01:05:27Z) is the earliest 'Starting' line still in the journal for that unit, and total all-time starts (305) is within one of the 30-minute count (304) — consistent with the loop beginning then, but journal rotation means this is a floor on the start time, not a proven origin.

Breaker states are a faithful replication of budget_allows() (including the legacy {B8:RY} signature mapping) executed against the live receipts file, not an invocation of the ops-agent itself — importing the live module could have side effects, so it was deliberately not executed.
Budget use is a point-in-time count of last-24h OPS_B_EXECUTED rows; it changes every tick (~5.5 min) and should be re-measured before any decision.
Board 182's memory figures moved between reads (875 MiB then 1526 MiB available) within ~6 minutes; the board is under active pressure.
No vault census was performed — that territory belongs to the parallel UNIFIED-RECON lane, so this lane reports VAULT_CENSUS=IN_PROGRESS_BY_OTHER_LANE.
Secret values were never printed: only paths, sizes, row counts, states and hashes.
The revenue-drive failure was diagnosed entirely from journal + unit file + script source; the fix was NOT applied (it is a mutation and out of scope).

REVISION 2 MATERIAL WEAKNESS, stated plainly: revision 1's board inventory was derived by hand from documents and memory instead of from the organism's own fleet registry, and PHASE 1 tested only two of the three SSH keys available. That produced two false UNREACHABLE labels and one missing node. The owner's question is what exposed it. Any downstream merge should treat revision 2's host list as authoritative and revision 1's as superseded.
Board 114's swap and NTP state were not read (only load, memory, disk, uptime and units were captured), so those two fields are honestly blank rather than assumed.

Board 180's second-pass drift sample (+1.122s at rtt 2.368s) is reported as-is rather than discarded; the pass-1 reading for the same host was +0.170s at rtt 0.460s, and the outlier is attributed to round-trip time.
